sections.html:
Kearney is the Buffalo County seat, built beside the Platte River on Interstate 80, with the Union Pacific main line through town. About 34,782 residents lived here as of July 1, 2025, and the city covers about 13 square miles. Health care, education, retail and manufacturing anchor the local economy.

The county reports an average commute of 16 minutes, so when you describe a house to a buyer, give the minutes to the interstate and to the university.

sections.h2: Renting near the University of Nebraska at Kearney
sections.html:
UNK is a 235-acre residential campus and one of the larger employers in the city. Central Community College also has a branch campus in Kearney. Homes near campus are often rentals.

  • If you own a rental, gather the leases and security deposit records before you talk to a buyer.
  • Give a buyer copies of the leases and deposit amounts early so nothing surprises them at closing.
  • Tenants stay in place unless the lease says otherwise, so check the end dates.

sections.h2: Weather and your roof, siding and concrete
sections.html:
Kearney averages 25.56 inches of precipitation and 21.8 inches of snow a year. May is the wettest month at 4.40 inches, and February is the snowiest at 5.6 inches. Hot summers and cold, dry winters stress roofing, siding and concrete flatwork, and a buyer's inspector will note all three.

If the house needs a roof or a furnace, get a written bid before you decide how to sell. It gives you a real number to weigh against a cash offer.

Kearney's Development Services Department handles permits, code enforcement, inspections and planning and zoning in one place. Building Services checks work against the adopted zoning, building, electrical and plumbing codes. Code Enforcement takes complaints by phone at (308) 233-3235 or through the Access Kearney app.

  • Ask whether past projects on your house were permitted.
  • Ask the department for open permits or violations on your address before you accept an offer.
  • The city code is on Municode if you want to read the chapters yourself.

Call the department to ask whether any sale-time inspection applies to your house.

sections.h2: Deeds, copies and property tax in Buffalo County
sections.html:
The Buffalo County Register of Deeds records deeds in the courthouse in Kearney, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. Copies cost $0.50 a page. The office also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that emails or texts you when a document is recorded under your name.

OfficeHandlesPhone
Register of DeedsDeed recording, copies, fraud alert(308) 236-1239
TreasurerProperty tax bills, tax sales (PO Box 1270, Kearney)(308) 236-1250
Code EnforcementComplaints, open violations(308) 233-3235

For delinquency dates, ask the Treasurer about your parcel. State law sets May 1 and September 1 in counties under 100,000 people.

sections.h2: Watch for the Recorded Deed Notice mailer
sections.html: A mail scam asks for $86 and calls itself a "Recorded Deed Notice." The Register of Deeds says to send no money. You can get a copy of your own recorded deed at the courthouse for $0.50 a page.

The seller pays the state documentary stamp tax when the deed is recorded. Under LB1067 it rises from $2.32 to $3.32 per $1,000 beginning July 18, 2026, and the higher rate runs through December 31, 2031. Budget for it as a closing cost.

sections.h2: The disclosure form and its timing
sections.html:
The disclosure statement must reach the buyer on or before the effective date of the binding contract, and the buyer must acknowledge receipt in writing. If you learn something before then that makes the statement wrong, update it.

Fill the form out at the start, not after you accept an offer. It covers appliances, the electrical, heating and cooling, water and sewer systems, defects that affect value, hazardous substances, title conditions and carbon monoxide alarm compliance.

A missed form does not void the transfer. The buyer can still sue for actual damages and attorney's fees, so complete it every time.

sections.h2: Preparing a Kearney house for buyers
sections.html:
Start with the things an inspector sees in the first ten minutes: roof, furnace, water heater, electrical panel and the concrete steps and drive. Fix cheap items yourself. For anything big, get one written bid so you know the real cost.

  • Collect warranties, receipts and permit records into one folder.
  • Check the house for open permits or code violations with Development Services.
  • Decide early whether you will repair, credit the buyer or sell as is.
  • If tenants live there, tell them a sale is coming and ask how they want showings handled.

A buyer paying cash usually inspects less and does not need a lender's repair list met, which can save weeks.

A title company or attorney runs a title search, clears liens, prorates the year's property tax and prepares the deed. You sign the deed, and the Register of Deeds records it at the courthouse. The state documentary stamp tax is paid when the deed is recorded, and the amount comes out of your proceeds.

Bring photo ID, the keys, garage openers and any remaining warranty papers. If you inherited the house, the court paperwork that gives you authority to sell goes to the title company ahead of time. The Property Fraud Alert from the Register of Deeds is worth signing up for after the sale, because it tells you if any document is later recorded under your name.

Property tax is billed by the Treasurer, and unpaid taxes are sold through tax sales. Pay or settle the current bill before closing so the title company has a clean number to work from.

A cash sale does not wait on an appraisal or a lender's underwriting, and it usually drops the repair-request round that follows a buyer's inspection. The disclosure form, the deed, the recording and the tax proration all still happen. Compare any cash offer with what you would net after commissions, repairs and the months of carrying costs a listing can bring. We do not promise a price, and you can ask for an offer without committing to anything.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in Kearney, Nebraska?
faqs.a: The Buffalo County Register of Deeds, in the county courthouse in Kearney. Call (308) 236-1239 or email deeds@buffalocounty.ne.gov.

faqs.q: What is the Nebraska documentary stamp tax rate for a Kearney sale?
faqs.a: It is $3.32 per $1,000 of value from July 18, 2026. The increase runs through December 31, 2031.

faqs.q: What is the Recorded Deed Notice scam in Buffalo County?
faqs.a: It is a mailer that asks for about $86 for a copy of a recorded deed. Copies cost $0.50 a page at the courthouse, and you should not send money.

faqs.q: Does Kearney require a point-of-sale inspection for a house?
faqs.a: Call Kearney Development Services at the number on the city's code enforcement page to confirm.

faqs.q: Which school district covers most of Kearney?
faqs.a: Kearney Public Schools, which operates preschools, ten elementary schools, two middle schools and Kearney High School.
